 Reeling Jets regress in blowout loss to Chiefs 
 By 
 Mark Cannizzaro 
 Published 
 Nov. 8, 2026, 4:12 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make New York Post a Preferred Source 
 KANSAS CITY — Directly adjacent to the entrance to Arrowhead Stadium is the “Faith & Family Chapel, Presented by Life Church.’’
 The makeshift chapel, which is mere steps away from the entrances to the stadium, sounded like it was bustling on the inside some two hours before the Jets and Chiefs kicked off Sunday.
 Take flight with the Jets 
 Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off. 
 tRY IT NOW 
 Perhaps the Jets should have stopped in there as a group before boarding the team buses for the airport after they were waxed 35-12 by the Chiefs.
 Because prayer might be the only thing that can now save their season, which has spiraled to a 2-7 record and counting as they lost their fourth consecutive game.
 “Lot of thinking to do,” Jets embattled head coach Aaron Glenn said, sounding like a coach who’s run out of answers as his reeling team continues to make the same mistakes week after week — killer third-down penalties, failure to score TDs in the red zone, defensive breakdowns and on and on.
 5 
 Kansas City Chiefs defensive end Ashton Gillotte (97) sacks New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (7) during a game in Kansas City, Mo., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

 The lasting images from this game, which the Jets trailed just 14-12 at the half after they dominated the Chiefs but continued to let them off the hook by settling for field goals instead of touchdowns, was the frustration shown by some of their key players.
 Geno Smith, after being sacked in the fourth quarter on a fourth-down play, slammed the ball to the ground, screamed at teammates and, when he came to the sideline, threw his helmet into the bench.
 “Just frustrated with not getting it done,’’ Smith said later after he was 18-for-32 passing for 165 yards.
 Later in the fourth quarter, after right tackle Armand Membou gave up a bad sack to end another series on fourth down, he slammed his helmet and drew a penalty and then, when he got to the sideline, threw his helmet against the bench and laid waste to an electronic tablet, spiking it into the ground.
 5 
 Kansas City Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton (32) forces a fumble on New York Jets running back Braelon Allen (0) on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, in Kansas City, Mo. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 
 5 
 New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn stands on the field before a game against the Kansas City Chiefs in Kansas City, Missouri, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 
 “I don’t like losing,” was Membou’s terse response after the game about the outburst.
 Unfortunately then, Membou, who played his college ball at nearby Missouri, was drafted by the wrong team. Because there’s a lot of losing going on with the Jets, and has been for a long time now.
 On this day, no one needed safety Minkah Fitzpatrick to say what it sounded like he said after last week’s loss to the Raiders (though he clarified it later as something else).

 This was, indeed, a classic case of Jets being Jets. They dominated the first half, and absolutely should have been winning the game. Story of the season.
 The Jets ran 39 offensive plays in the first half to 24 for the Chiefs and had possession for 20:26 to 9:34. Twenty-five of those 39 Jets offensive plays came on the Kansas City side of the field. But they settled for Jason Sanders field goals of 23, 48, 49 and 53 yards.
 5 
 New York Jets defensive tackle T’vondre Sweat trips Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III during a game on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, in Kansas City, Mo. Getty Images 
 Kicking field goals against an explosive Kansas City offense led by quarterback Patrick Mahomes (two TD passes), running back Kenneth Walker (three TDs, one rushing and two receiving) and tight end Travis Kelce (one TD) is like trying to win a gunfight with a squirt gun.
 This formula was never going to work for the Jets.
 Their formula for the second half was even worse, though, as the Jets ran 23 plays for 58 yards on five possessions that ended in punts three times and downs twice.
 Conversely, the Chiefs ran 41 plays for 257 yards in the second half and outscored the Jets 21-0.
 “It’s disappointing, and I told our players that,” Glenn said. “We’ve shown in spurts that we can play at a high level.”
 Those “spurts,” though, are far too infrequent, with little sustainability.
 The Jets had a chance to add a spark to their sagging season on Sunday, playing against one of the NFL’s elite teams. They had a chance to ignite a flicker of life into 2026, a glimmer of hope.
 5 
 Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Kristian Fulton tackles New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, in Kansas City, Mo. AP Photo/Ed Zurga 
 Instead, they regressed, made the same mistakes they’ve been making all season, only more of them.
 So, the beat goes on for Glenn, whose team next plays the AFC East-leading 6-1 Bills Sunday at MetLife Stadium. That makes 2-8 highly likely after playing the Bills, who are a 7½-point favorite.
 Sure, the Jets were 9½-point underdogs to the Chiefs. But when — if ever — is Glenn going to deliver anything that resembles a “signature” victory? The Jets are now 5-21 in his tenure as head coach, numbers that are inching dangerously close to Kotite-ian figures. With numbers like that, prayer may be the only thing that has a chance to save the season and Glenn’s job.
